messages:
anya: Quick check — ran into a weird edge case while validating the new sampling fallback. When a stop sequence overlaps the max_tokens cutoff, are we guaranteeing that the returned text includes the stop tokens in the streamed chunks? I'm seeing truncation and logprobs that don't line up.

sam_k: Can you paste the request you used? top_p/temp/max_tokens ordering can change behaviour across runtime versions.

anya: Sure — minimal repro: 
```json
POST /v1/generate
{
  \"model\": \"redwood-alpha-1\",
  \"input\": \"Write a haiku about clouds\",
  \"max_tokens\": 10,
  \"stop\": [\"\\n\"],
  \"temperature\": 0.0,
  \"top_p\": 0.9,
  \"logprobs\": 2,
  \"stream\": true
}
```
Output (streamed chunks):
- chunk1: \"Write a haiku about clouds\nclouds drift across the\"
- chunk2 (truncated): \" sky\" /* stop sequence should cut here */
Final payload shows stop not present and logprobs array length shorter than tokens.

kai: Hmm. Two things to confirm: 1) Are you using a pinned model version or the floating alias? 2) Is the KV-cache off for this run? Streaming + caching + early stop can cause partial chunking differences.

anya: Pinned to v2026-03-10, KV cache disabled. Also tried with stream=false and saw final response also missing the stop tokens sometimes (they're not in the returned text, but reason: \"stop\" appears in the metadata).

maria_pm: Is this a contract-breaker for product? If stops can disappear, some downstream parsers will break. We should make a compatibility decision.

sam_k: From the API contract side: we guarantee that the model will stop at the earliest occurrence of any stop sequence and that the user-visible text should not include the stop sequence itself (i.e., we strip it). But the streaming chunks behavior is allowed to emit partial context before we learn we hit stop. Key is final assembled text and token/logprob alignment.

anya: Right — in my case final assembled text doesn't look like we stripped the stop (it seems we truncated before it and didn't include it). The logprobs array also has fewer entries than final tokens which breaks our token-level evaluation.

devex: Related note: we've had small regressions when temperature=0 + top_p<1.0 because we transform to greedy with nucleus sampling fallback; different codepath can produce disparity in how we compute logprobs. Could be a bug where logprob indexing assumes greedy path.

kai: Can you run with top_p=1.0 and temp=0.0 and compare? If top_p<1.0 and temp=0 then some implementations coerce to deterministic sampling by selecting highest cumulative prob until p >= top_p — that changes which tokens are considered and affects logprobs shape.

anya: Ran both: with top_p=1.0 + temp=0.0 final text includes the stop consistently and logprobs align. With top_p=0.9 + temp=0.0 we get the mismatch.

sam_k: OK that's actionable: we should document that (temp=0 && top_p<1) triggers nucleus deterministic path and may have different streaming/logprob behavior. But ideally we keep final contract stable: final text, token count, and logprobs length must match. If current runtime breaks that, file a bug.

maria_pm: Filing a bug + impact. If this is a contract regression we should consider a micropatch release for Dedicated customers.

ml-bot: ISSUE created #4527: \"logprob/token alignment when temp=0 & top_p<1 causes truncated stop sequence in final output\" — linked to thread.

anya: Thanks — adding a small repro test in the gen-tests suite and a CI smoke that asserts: len(tokens) == len(logprobs) and final_text does not contain partial stop prefix.

devex: Also please add a note in the API docs caveat section about deterministic/coerced sampling modes. We should avoid customers being surprised by different code paths.

sam_k: For the runtime fix: likely off-by-one in the streaming finalizer when early-stopping and using nucleus-select. I'll take a look and ping for code review — PR incoming (sam/fix-stop-align).

anya: Ping me on the PR for review, will attach the failing snippet and CI reproduction. :eyes:

kai: One more quick question for the patch — if we're stripping stop tokens in final_text, do we also guarantee that the last token's logprob corresponds to the last emitted token pre-strip? i.e., if the stop is stripped, do we include logprob for the token before stop or include stop token logprob? We need to be explicit.

sam_k: Contract: logprobs list aligns with tokens the SDK returns in the text field (post-processing). We should not return logprobs for the stripped stop token. I'll add that to the PR description and the API docs.

maria_pm: Great. TL;DR action items: sam to PR + include regression test, anya to add smoke test to gen-tests, devex to update docs caveat, ops to consider hotfix for Dedicated if root cause is runtime. :thumbsup:

anya: I'll drop the test and example into the PR branch and link. Thanks everyone.

sam_k: PR created: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pull/1376 — includes fix + tests.

anya: Verified on staging — behavior fixed for my repro. Will run broader testset tonight and report back.

maria_pm: Thanks. Keep this thread updated with rollout ETA if all green.
